question: why do the llama and deepseek2 adapters return degenerate tokens

bisect.method: generate exactly one token, which separates the forward pass from the decode loop, KV reuse and sampling
bisect.conclusion: both failing families are already wrong at the first forward, so the defect is upstream of decode

false_lead_1.claim: dispatches_per_forward == 0 shows Metal is never reached
false_lead_1.why: the counter is assigned only in qwen_dense.rs:2207; deepseek_v2.rs has 136 Metal call sites and llama.rs 24

false_lead_2.claim: the llama golden hash mismatch is a code regression
false_lead_2.found: the smoke test failed with golden b349ac717a98318a against a measured ee12bbd4b09c558f, pinned at 34c31541 'fix(rope): interleaved -> NEOX pairing'

commits_examined.9463d333 (my rustfmt): CLEARED, the llama.rs diff is import reordering and line joining only
commits_examined.dee10fde share model helpers: CLEARED, rmsnorm_dispatch and gemv_f16_dispatch are faithful to the inline code they replaced

false_lead_2.why_withdrawn: the control I nearly skipped: the golden pins no input identity. It records a token hash with no publisher, sha256 or quant level, while the finder accepts any models/*llama-3.2-1b*.gguf. Two publishers' Q4_K_M of one model give different tokens for reasons that are nobody's bug, so the mismatch cannot distinguish a regression from a different file.

real_finding.defect: the golden gate is unsound as written: it pins an output without pinning the input
real_finding.consequence: it can neither prove a regression nor rule one out, and it has been skipping since 2026-06-22 for want of weights, so nothing noticed
real_finding.fix: the baseline key now carries the weights sha256 prefix and byte size, so drift on a given file is real drift and a different file gets its own entry instead of a false failure

still_unexplained: why llama and deepseek2 are wrong at the first forward. The bisect narrows it to the forward pass; the cause is not identified and is not guessed at here.
lesson: two inferences in one investigation rested on an unpinned default: a counter only one adapter sets, and a golden that does not name its input. Both looked like evidence.
